per_run_differences.note: The V2 script adds gradient checkpointing, use_cache=False and a paged 8-bit optimizer so the 46-trajectory run fits the same 15GB T4 budget. This does not affect E4 (V1 adapter held constant, parser only), but it means the E4->V2 contrast changes the training run and not only the training data. The v2 script comments note that max_seq_length is ignored in trl>=0.14; the trl version used for the v1 run was not recorded.

training_config.prior_corrections: README vs reproducibility.md previously disagreed (alpha=32 vs alpha=16; full attn vs attn-only). Fixed after checking adapter_config.json — both v1 and v2 used alpha=16, attention-only. A second correction (2026-10) removed the claim that v1 and v2 shared an identical optimizer/gradient-checkpointing configuration.

e4_lora_fixed_parser.notes: Controlled ablation: V1 adapter + V2 parser. Tavily real API. Per-task traces not captured.

confound.label: PARTIALLY RESOLVED by E4
confound.statement: E4 (V1 adapter + V2 parser = 18/23) isolates the parser effect from the training-run effect. Parser aggregate effect = E4 - V1 = 0 tasks. The remaining E4->V2 difference is +5 tasks, and that transition changes the adapter, the training data, and the V2 run's optimizer/gradient-checkpointing settings together.
confound.residual_confound: training/colab_train_7b_v2.py additionally enables gradient checkpointing, use_cache=False and a paged 8-bit optimizer; colab_train_7b.py does not. See training_config.per_run_differences.
confound.resolution_evidence: E4 controlled ablation completed 2026-09-16 on Colab T4 with real Tavily API. Same V1 adapter weights, same benchmark, different parser. Score unchanged at 18/23.
